newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin wants joint border patrols with Finns.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin wants joint border patrols with Finns.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Saturday he planned to suggest to Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari during two days of talks that Russia and Finland jointly patrol their long border to save money.

He told reporters before Ahtisaari flew in to join him at his holiday retreat in northwest Russia that he would also propose opening up 13 islands in the Gulf of Finland that have been off-limits to Finns since the 1950s.
"How much money do we waste on border activities? And how much do they waste, too?" Yeltsin said in his remarks to reporters.
"Look, we are two presidents, let's get together. Let's look after the border jointly -- it will be half the price."
Russia is battling to reform and cut the size of its armed forces to make them more efficient and to reduce the country's budget deficit.
It was not immediately clear whether Ahtisaari would back the proposal to mount joint patrols along the border.

Yeltsin said he was prepared to open access to islands declared closed to Finns in 1956 during the Soviet era. He said he would propose jointly developing one or two of the islands as tourist centres and splitting the profits with Finland.
Yeltsin said he was enjoying his holiday in the deep forests of Karelia. He was swimming every day in the lake in front of his residence and then taking a Russian "banya" steam bath to warm up.

Itar-Tass news agency reported earlier that Yeltsin had played tennis -- his favourite sport -- for the first time since he underwent heart surgery last November. It said he put in some training on the court for about 10 minutes on Friday.
